reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure; zero dimension is permitted. Let mu be any probability measure. For any real b,eta,tau with b>=0,eta>=0,tau>0 and any u, let rho be mu reweighted by exp(-(b/2)*norm(x-u)^2) and normalized by its integral. Let S_s(P) be the actual law of X+sZ under P times the centered identity-covariance standard Gaussian. Then rho is probability and S_sqrt(tau)(S_sqrt(eta)(rho))=S_sqrt(eta+tau)(rho). There exists one measurable Markov kernel K such that for every y, K(y) is rho reweighted by exp(-norm(x-y)^2/(2*(eta+tau))) and normalized by its rho integral. The exact measure identity K composed with S_sqrt(tau)(S_sqrt(eta)(rho))=rho holds. Kernel composition with P assigns each measurable B the integral K(y,B) dP(y), and each fiber is probability. The same K simultaneously satisfies for every probability nu and real r>=0: if W2(nu,S_sqrt(eta)(rho))<=ofReal(r), then actual KL(K composed with S_sqrt(tau)(nu),rho)<=ofReal(r^2/(2*tau)). W2(P,Q) is the extended-nonnegative square root of the actual infimum over measures Gamma whose first marginal is P and second is Q of the extended-nonnegative integral of ofReal(norm(x-y)^2). No separate second-moment hypothesis on either marginal is imposed. The divergence direction is reconstructed output relative to rho. Actual ENNReal KL for probability laws equals ofReal(integral log((dP/dQ).toReal) dP) when P is absolutely continuous relative to Q and that logarithm is P-integrable, and infinity otherwise. Neither absolute continuity nor log-integrability is an extra premise. K may depend on E,mu,b,eta,tau,u but is chosen before nu,r. Its fiber formula is everywhere, not only almost everywhere. Its tilt uses total eta+tau, while the bound uses added tau exactly, coefficient1/(2*tau). Only the anonymous statement and approved definitions were used; no source-fidelity or compilation judgment.
